I don't think this target can pass the axiom check, but here is my best restatement. Both failures report `sorryAx`. The cause appears to be that `binarySyndromeDecodingPromise` has `disjoint := by sorry`. Any theorem whose statement mentions that definition, including the original side of the `↔` that we assemble, then depends on `sorryAx`. A restatement cannot remove that dependency. I have not been able to run Lean here, so the proof below is untested.

The restatement below unfolds `IsNPHardPromise` and `PromiseReduction` into explicit quantifiers. It does not mention the promise problem, but the proof still unfolds it.

{"mode":"iff","restated":"∀ language : BitLanguage, IsNP language = true → ∃ map : List Bool → List Bool, Nonempty (BitTM map) ∧ (∀ input : List Bool, language input = true → ∃ record : BinarySyndromeDecodingInstance, encodeBinarySyndromeDecodingInstance record = map input ∧ 0 < record.blockLength ∧ 0 < record.radius ∧ ∃ word : Fin record.blockLength → ZMod 2, binarySyndromeProduct record word = binarySyndromeTarget record ∧ hammingNorm word ≤ record.radius) ∧ (∀ input : List Bool, ¬ (language input = true) → ∃ record : BinarySyndromeDecodingInstance, encodeBinarySyndromeDecodingInstance record = map input ∧ 0 < record.blockLength ∧ 0 < record.radius ∧ (∃ word : Fin record.blockLength → ZMod 2, binarySyndromeProduct record word = binarySyndromeTarget record) ∧ ∀ word : Fin record.blockLength → ZMod 2, binarySyndromeProduct record word = binarySyndromeTarget record → binaryCodeGapFactor record.blockLength * (record.radius : ℝ) < (hammingNorm word : ℝ))","proof":"unfold IsNPHardPromise
simp only [decide_eq_true_eq]
constructor
· intro h language hl
  obtain ⟨R⟩ := h language hl
  refine ⟨R.map, R.polynomial_time, ?_, ?_⟩
  · intro input hin
    have := R.completeness input hin
    simpa only [binarySyndromeDecodingPromise, decide_eq_true_eq] using this
  · intro input hin
    have := R.soundness input hin
    simpa only [binarySyndromeDecodingPromise, decide_eq_true_eq] using this
· intro h language hl
  obtain ⟨map, hp, hc, hs⟩ := h language hl
  exact ⟨{ map := map, polynomial_time := hp, completeness := fun input hin => by simpa only [binarySyndromeDecodingPromise, decide_eq_true_eq] using hc input hin, soundness := fun input hin => by simpa only [binarySyndromeDecodingPromise, decide_eq_true_eq] using hs input hin }⟩","english":"Every language in NP has a polynomial-time computable map on bit strings that sends each input to the encoding of a binary syndrome-decoding instance. If the input is in the language, the instance is a YES instance: some word of Hamming weight at most the radius has syndrome equal to the target. If the input is not in the language, the instance is a NO instance: it is consistent (some word has the target syndrome), and every word with that syndrome has Hamming weight greater than n^(1/200) times the radius, where n is the block length.","why_clearer":"It unfolds the opaque Bool-valued `decide` encodings and the `PromiseReduction` structure into explicit quantifiers over instances, words and weights."}

parsed.proof:
unfold IsNPHardPromise
simp only [decide_eq_true_eq]
constructor
· intro h language hl
  obtain ⟨R⟩ := h language hl
  refine ⟨R.map, R.polynomial_time, ?_, ?_⟩
  · intro input hin
    have := R.completeness input hin
    simpa only [binarySyndromeDecodingPromise, decide_eq_true_eq] using this
  · intro input hin
    have := R.soundness input hin
    simpa only [binarySyndromeDecodingPromise, decide_eq_true_eq] using this
· intro h language hl
  obtain ⟨map, hp, hc, hs⟩ := h language hl
  exact ⟨{ map := map, polynomial_time := hp, completeness := fun input hin => by simpa only [binarySyndromeDecodingPromise, decide_eq_true_eq] using hc input hin, soundness := fun input hin => by simpa only [binarySyndromeDecodingPromise, decide_eq_true_eq] using hs input hin }⟩
parsed.english: Every language in NP has a polynomial-time computable map on bit strings that sends each input to the encoding of a binary syndrome-decoding instance. If the input is in the language, the instance is a YES instance: some word of Hamming weight at most the radius has syndrome equal to the target. If the input is not in the language, the instance is a NO instance: it is consistent (some word has the target syndrome), and every word with that syndrome has Hamming weight greater than n^(1/200) times the radius, where n is the block length.
parsed.why_clearer: It unfolds the opaque Bool-valued `decide` encodings and the `PromiseReduction` structure into explicit quantifiers over instances, words and weights.
